decisions.statement: The files of every page in the tree are judged rather than a check's own code.
The page types a file may be named for are asked of the index.
A literal is judged by the path that literal reaches rather than by the text that literal spells.
A call the checkout's root flows into is a reach at the checkout.
A reach is found by the root flowing into the call rather than by the name the call has.
A call taking a root outside the checkout reaches no path this check judges.
A page's code spelling a page file's name where that code lists is refused.
A name is a page file's where a page type the index knows sits between its dots.
What follows that page type in the name is a run of plain segments.
The index answers a file whose own name closes with that name.
A name the index answers no file for names nothing and is let through.
A name only a file held uncommitted carries names nothing and is let through.
A judgement here is the same over a checkout and over the overlay a deploy reads.
A name refused already as a path spelled is not refused a second time.
A page's test listing a folder is judged by no name that test spells.
A page type reached through a template rather than a plain string is not seen.
A reach whose root is built from anything but plain strings is not seen.
A literal reaching a directory listing is refused.
A literal naming a path the index has a page at is refused.
A folder above a page is no page.
A literal naming a folder is refused only where a listing reaches that literal.
A literal naming nothing the index answers for is let through.
A literal naming a page is refused once, at the line that literal sits on.
A path is spelled where the index knows a page at that path.
A path is spelled where the index knows a page under that path.
A path is spelled where the index knows a page ending with that path.
More than one page may end with the path spelled.
The page named is the one sharing the most folders with the file spelling it.
The first page the index answers is named where two share as many folders.
A page is named ahead of a folder wherever both end with the path spelled.
Which page is named changes nothing about which files are refused.
A literal ending in a separator names the folder that separator closes.
A name with no separator is no path.
A literal is read again from each separator in that literal.
A path spelled inside a longer literal is read like a literal spelling that path alone.
A literal is answered by the first reading the index answers for.
A run a shell variable opens names a place the shell picks at run time.
No reading of such a run is asked of the index.
A run whose own opening is spelled is asked though a variable fills a segment after it.
A reading opening with a dot is a reach from the folder the spelling file sits in.
A reading after the whole literal that opens with a dot is no reach.
A reach is resolved against that folder before the index is asked.
A reach is answered by the path it lands on rather than by a path ending with it.
A reach climbing above the tree lands nowhere.
A reading opening with a separator names no path.
A specifier opening with a dot is a specifier rather than a reach.
An expression has whatever a name inside that expression carries.
A name carries whatever an initializer of that name has.
Whatever a name carries is worked out again until nothing changes.
A name a loop binds has whatever the source that loop runs over carries.
A name a `for in` loop binds is a key rather than whatever that loop runs over.
A name carries over the whole file rather than within the scope that name is bound in.
One listing is refused once however many arguments of that listing have a path.
Every string a body has is read rather than the specifiers alone.
A specifier is left to the checks that judge a specifier.
Which literals name a module is answered by the module named here.
A page file written in TypeScript is judged where that file is the page's code or test.
A page's code is every file of that page whose last section is `code`.
A page's test is every file of that page whose last section is `test`.
A fixture builds a tree of its own, so no path a fixture spells is judged.
A page file written in another language is judged whatever section names that file.
A file no page claims is judged by nothing here.
An index's own code is run by the rebuild that writes the index.
A file the index is built from spells its own path rather than asking the index.
An index's own code is judged by nothing here.
A file held uncommitted is judged by nothing here.
A file a page property says a machine writes is judged by nothing here.
A file a page property says a tool resolves the paths in is judged by nothing here.
A body whose language is not parsed is read as the runs of path characters that body holds.
Such a run is read again from each separator in that run.
A run naming a path the index has a page at is refused.
One run is refused once, at the line that run sits on.
A body outside TypeScript holds no listing.
A body that is no text is read as the text a decoder gives.
The refusal names the line the listing sits on and the path the index answered.
A long reading is shortened where the refusal names that reading.
A path built from anything but plain strings is not seen.
A value a helper returns is not carried to the caller that lists that value.
A path the index knows no page for is seen by nothing here.
A run in prose that spells a page's path is refused like a run meant as a path.
A pattern the bundler reads before the code runs is no reach at the checkout.
A folder the tree search holds apart is a folder the shadow answers no path under.
A reach under a folder the search holds apart is judged by nothing here.
A file named for a check's audit is judged by nothing here.
The code the shadow's surface reaches through its imports is judged by nothing here.
That code is worked out from the import graph rather than from a list of paths.
A reach past the shadow in a check's own code is refused.
A reach is found without a list of reader names.
`filesIn` handed the shadow's root is a reach this check refuses.
The shadow lists the folders sitting in a folder.
This page is named for the overlay rather than for the index.

definition: the check refusing a page file that spells or lists a path the index answers for
